biography: Shane 'SVG' van Gisbergen hails from Auckland, New Zealand, a land steeped in motorsport history. Growing up surrounded by the roar of engines at his father's local garage, Shane was practically born behind the wheel. His karting career was meteoric, punctuated by a national championship at the tender age of 14. A daring move to Australia's V8 Supercars followed soon after, where he quickly established himself as a prodigious talent. While moments of brilliance showcased his raw speed, occasional clashes with rivals and a tendency to over-drive plagued his early years. Now, entering what most consider his peak years, Shane is determined to harness his natural ability into consistent championship contention. A switch to high-performance GT cars with Brabham and a foray into stock car racing in the USA reflects a drive to test his limits across different racing disciplines, seeking the ultimate challenge.
drivingStyle: Van Gisbergen's driving style can be best described as aggressive and instinctive. He's known for his late braking maneuvers and daring overtakes, often threading the needle where others wouldn't dare. While this approach yields spectacular results, it can also lead to costly mistakes. He's continually working on refining his tire management skills, recognizing that consistent pace trumps outright speed over the course of a race. Under pressure, SVG tends to become even more aggressive, sometimes to his detriment, but when he nails it, it's poetry in motion.

rivalries.reason: A heated rivalry stemming from a controversial last-lap collision at Bathurst in 2022, where Bellini accused Van Gisbergen of intentionally wrecking him to secure the win.
A fierce on-track battle for championship points in the Stock USA Gen3 series, characterized by numerous close calls and aggressive blocking maneuvers.
A clash of personalities and driving styles in Team Avalone. Tanaka, valuing precision and data, often clashed with Van Gisbergen's more instinctual approach.

quirks: Always wears a specific faded t-shirt under his race suit, a lucky charm from his karting days.
Listens to heavy metal, particularly Pantera, to pump himself up before a race.
Has a habit of sketching track layouts in the dirt with his finger while doing his pre-race walk.
famousQuote: "You can't win if you're not willing to risk it all. Second place is just the first loser."
careerHighlight: Winning the Bathurst 1000 in 2022 after a nail-biting final stint, holding off Marco Bellini in a damaged car to secure his first major endurance victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the 2020 Supercars championship decider due to a mechanical failure, handing the title to his rival.
